metadata.title: He-star donor pathway for the hypervelocity star D6-2

evidence.quote: Our models showed that the hot subdwarf + white dwarf channel can plausibly explain the properties of D6-2.
He-star donor pathway for the hypervelocity star D6–2
The recent discovery of hypervelocity white dwarfs by Shen et al. (2018) provides potential observational evidence for surviving companions of Type Ia supernova explosions.
One of these candidates (D6-2) even traces back to a faint supernova remnant, reinforcing the ejection hypothesis.
Our models showed that the hot subdwarf + white dwarf channel can plausibly explain the properties of D6-2.

values.condition: Approximate (∼) observed total velocity of D6-2 quoted from previous studies (Shen et al. 2018; El-Badry et al. 2023); the paper does not decompose it into components or state the frame explicitly beyond it being the star's observed (ejection/total) velocity.

evidence.quote: Given that D6–2 is observed at a velocity of ∼1000 km s−1
They identify three candidate stars with total velocities between ∼1000 km s−1 and 3000 km s−1
The grey region shows the velocity range observed for D6-2.

The hypervelocity He-rich star US 708 (Hirsch et al. 2005) has been explained as the runaway donor star from a thermonuclear explosion (Justham et al. 2009; Geier et al. 2015; Brown et al. 2015; Neunteufel et al. 2022).

The hypervelocity He-rich star US 708 (Hirsch et al. 2005) has been explained as the runaway donor star from a thermonuclear explosion (Justham et al. 2009; Geier et al. 2015; Brown et al. 2015; Neunteufel et al. 2022).

The orbital velocities of donor stars in this progenitor channel naturally yield orbital velocities consistent with US 708, LP 40–365 stars, and D6-2, indicating that a single class of thermonuclear supernova progenitors can account for their entire range of ejection velocities.
Our models also predict a good fraction of runaway stars with high core He fractions, up to 0.8, which could potentially account for objects like US 708.

notes: D6-2: The paper uses both D6–2 (T:p1-b0) and D6-2 (T:p6-b9) for the same object; the dash variation is typographic. Shen et al. (2018) had already identified it among three hypervelocity white-dwarf candidates, but only D6-2 is named in the supplied text (T:p4-b6); this paper follows it up with velocity and composition modeling (T:p6-b9). US 708: Included as a previously known hypervelocity star used for model comparison (T:p1-b9; T:p6-b11), not as a newly selected candidate. LP 40–365: The text refers only to the plural class “LP 40–365 stars” (T:p7-b4) and does not identify individual members, so the group is not expanded into star entries.

D6-2: The paper gives no right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability for D6-2; it only refers qualitatively to D6-2's compact, faint, low-temperature state and to its observed velocity. The velocity is quoted only approximately (∼1000 km/s) in the text ('the velocity of D6-2, reported by Shen et al. (2018)' and 'the measured velocity of D6-2' in the Fig. 2 caption). The grey D6-2 bands in Figs. 1, 2 and 6 are described only qualitatively and their plotted edges (∼1000 to the plot limits) are not stated numerically in the text, so no interval is recorded (see T:p2-b1, T:p3-b0, T:p6-b0 and images I:p2-b1, I:p3-b0, I:p6-b0).

US 708: The target identifier is US 708. The paper discusses US 708 only qualitatively: it is mentioned as an example of a hypervelocity He-rich runaway donor from a thermonuclear explosion (T:p1-b9), as a system whose orbital velocities are consistent with this progenitor channel (T:p1-b6), and as an object that could be accounted for by models predicting runaway stars with core He fractions up to 0.8 (T:p6-b11). No numerical values (position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound probabilities) are reported for US 708; all quantitative results in the paper pertain to D6-2 and to the model population. Therefore no quantities are extracted for US 708.
